name: Question 3
problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=5{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}(t)-2{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -4\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform to both sides of each equation, we get the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{{field-1}}=5{X}_{1}(s) \\ {{field-2}}={{field-3}}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}$ are the Laplace transforms of the functions ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t),$ respectively.
worked_solution:
First, we find the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}L{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)}=L{5{x}_{1}(t)} \\ L{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)}=L{{x}_{1}(t)-2{x}_{2}(t)}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}sL{{x}_{1}(t)}-{x}_{1}(0)=5L{{x}_{1}(t)} \\ sL{{x}_{2}(t)}-{x}_{2}(0)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}-2L{{x}_{2}(t)}\end{aligned}
$$

which can be simplified to the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)+3=5{X}_{1}(s) \\ s{X}_{2}(s)+4={X}_{1}(s)-2{X}_{2}(s)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}$ are the Laplace transforms of the functions ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t),$ respectively.

EXPLANATION

First, we find the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

{L{x1′(t)}=L{5x1(t)}L{x2′(t)}=L{x1(t)−2x2(t)}

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

{sL{x1(t)}−x1(0)=5L{x1(t)}sL{x2(t)}−x2(0)=L{x1(t)}−2L{x2(t)}

which can be simplified to the following:

{sX1(s)+3=5X1(s)sX2(s)+4=X1(s)−2X2(s)

where X1(s)=L{x1(t)} and X2(s)=L{x2(t)} are the Laplace transforms of the functions x1(t) and x2(t), respectively.
